summary: Deployed a Python http.server app on node2:8080, terminated a WireGuard tunnel on node1 (wg0, 10.200.0.1/24, UDP 51820) with node3 as the sole peer (10.200.0.2/32), and used VyOS NAT+forward-filter on node1 to masquerade WireGuard-tunneled traffic destined for node2 as node1's LAN IP. node2's firewalld restricts TCP/8080 to source 10.100.47.10/32 (node1 only), so node3 can reach the app only via the tunnel through node1, never directly. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time per the mandatory protocol; each showed a changed OS boot_id and fully recovered app/tunnel/firewall state, with WireGuard handshakes re-establishing automatically afterward.
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes: node1=VyOS router, node2/node3=AlmaLinux 9.6, all sharing one provisioned /24 (10.100.47.0/24) — treated node3 as logically 'outside' via firewall+tunnel enforcement rather than physical L2 separation
Deployed and enabled a systemd-managed Python http.server on node2:8080 (app8080.service)
Installed wireguard-tools on node3; generated WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3 via `wg genkey`/`wg pubkey`

Configured VyOS wg0 on node1 (address 10.200.0.1/24, port 51820, peer node3 allowed-ips 10.200.0.2/32), a NAT source rule masquerading 10.200.0.0/24 -> 10.100.47.11 via eth0, a forward-filter (default-drop) with explicit accept for wg0->eth0 tcp/8080 to node2 plus established/related state, and an input-filter allow for UDP/51820; committed and saved
Restricted node2's firewalld to allow TCP/8080 only from source 10.100.47.10/32 (node1) via a dedicated zone; confirmed port 8080 was never opened on the public zone
Configured wg-quick@wg0 client on node3 (address 10.200.0.2/24, AllowedIPs limited to node2's IP plus the WG subnet, PersistentKeepalive 25) pointed at node1's WAN IP:51820; enabled and started it

Verified node3 could NOT reach node2:8080 directly before the tunnel was up ('No route to host'), and could reach it successfully once the WireGuard tunnel was active, with node2's access log showing the source as node1's LAN IP (10.100.47.10) and node1's conntrack table showing the NAT translation from 10.200.0.2 (node3 over WG) to 10.100.47.10 toward node2 — proving the app is reachable only via the tunnel terminated on node1
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id + service/tunnel/firewall health) on all three nodes

Restarted node1 (VyOS) via `reboot`; polled until exec responded again, confirmed boot_id changed (5bcff8f9... -> c03ea166...), verified wg0/NAT/firewall config persisted across reboot, forced a fresh WireGuard handshake from node3, and confirmed node3 could again reach node2:8080 through the tunnel

Restarted node2 (AlmaLinux) via `reboot`; polled until exec responded again, confirmed boot_id changed (e31962a9... -> 1c392c1c...), verified app8080.service active and firewalld node1only zone config persisted, and confirmed node3 could again reach node2:8080 through the tunnel

Restarted node3 (AlmaLinux) via `reboot`; polled until exec responded again, confirmed boot_id changed (54bd1c3e... -> b572dc15...), verified wg-quick@wg0 active, forced/confirmed a fresh handshake via ping to 10.200.0.1, and confirmed node3 could again reach node2:8080 through the tunnel

evidence.requirement: Application served from node2 on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: firewalld/python3 present on node2; app8080.service created, enabled, and confirmed listening on 0.0.0.0:8080

evidence.requirement: node3 cannot reach node2:8080 directly (outside the private network)
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to node2:8080 before/without the tunnel returns 'No route to host', confirming direct access is blocked by node2's firewalld source restriction

evidence.requirement: WireGuard tunnel from node3 terminated on node1
evidence.summary: wg0 configured on node1 (address, port, peer, NAT, firewall) and committed/saved; wg-quick@wg0 configured and started on node3; wg show confirms handshake and interface state on both ends

evidence.requirement: node3 reaches node2:8080 only via the tunnel through node1
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to node2:8080 succeeds once WireGuard is up; node2's access log shows the request source as node1's LAN IP (10.100.47.10), and node1's conntrack table shows the NAT translation from node3's tunnel IP (10.200.0.2) to node1's LAN IP toward node2, proving the enforced path

evidence.requirement: node2 firewalld restricts port 8080 to node1 only
evidence.summary: firewalld zone 'node1only' created with source 10.100.47.10/32 and port 8080/tcp; port was never enabled on the public zone

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9-...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect (connection reset confirms disconnect); boot_id changed to c03ea166-...; wg0/NAT/firewall config verified intact post-reboot; fresh WG handshake forced and node3->node2:8080 access verified working again

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id e31962a9-8d32-4c19-8dd2-0b96a45c6c48 (captured together with node1/node3 baseline call cmd-3d867baaed0a4ab6); reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 1c392c1c-e6f1-4dc7-be8a-6ff3a2478e16; app8080.service and firewalld node1only zone verified active post-reboot; node3->node2:8080 access verified working again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 54bd1c3e-3a1b-4913-841b-88512119e096; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to b572dc15-68b4-4fd2-b236-283cee73796b; wg-quick@wg0 verified active, fresh handshake confirmed via ping to 10.200.0.1, and node2:8080 access via the tunnel verified working again
